newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK manufacturing output, PPI data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK manufacturing output, PPI data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK data showing April manufacturing output rose 0.6% MM, 2.3% YY while May input prices were down 9.1% YY and May output prices were up 1.0% YY:
"Certainly on the manufacturing side it indicates that the strength of sterling has yet to have an impact on manufacturing production."

"It really vindicates the Bank of England's decision last Friday to raise interest rates by 25 basis points. On the industrial production side, there is probably an element of a bounceback in utility production. It's certainly the manufacturing numbers which catch the eye."

"The impact of sterling has yet to be seen fully in the manufacturing sector. Going forward, I think strength of this level on a month on month change in manufacturing output isn't really sustainable."
"The significant recovery in manufacturing figures is a surprise for markets and focuses on the current strength of the economy."
"Data showed a slightly more robust picture of economic growth and a steady price outlook which may be a small positive feature for the pound and a small negative for the interest rate markets."

BRIAN HILLIARD, SOCIETE GENERALE "It's a pretty good combination -- manufacturing output a bit stronger than expected, but inflation well under control. The price figures might show that the best is over, but the cost pressures are still very muted. There were no real problems on the output side either. Manufacturers are able to increase output in the face of strong sterling, and the production costs are still under control. It also shows there is no reason to raise retail prices. Prices are likely to remnain very competitive."
